deliverable: A source-grounded comparison of two short videos' explanations of binary floating-point error and mitigation advice (why 0.1 + 0.2 drifts, what IEEE 754 truncation does, and when to use integers for money), with a claim table, exact section locators, and explicit coverage gaps.

turns.text: Using only these two Douyin pages, compare how they explain floating-point imprecision: the Python π video's account of binary floats and the 0.1 / 0.1 + 0.2 drift, and the 浮点数、字符与常量本质 video's account of IEEE 754 mantissa truncation and its settlement advice. Cite each claim by page title and section heading (合集简介 episode or 章节要点), and keep the two sources separate.

Focus on the mechanism each page offers rather than on advice. What does the Python page say about how a float is stored and why 0.1 cannot be written exactly in binary, and what does the IEEE 754 page say about truncation and error accumulation? Cite the exact section for each statement, and flag any point where one page stops short of the mechanism the other gives.

List the gaps and disagreements between the two pages: does either page quantify the error, do they agree on the cause, and what practical advice appears on one page only (for example avoiding floats in financial settlement, or the character-type bit-flip point)? Say plainly what these captured page texts cannot support and whether the two videos are answering the same question.
